criteria.build_driving_ops: Design, implement, qualify and document new Can runtime surface for the blocked legs first: externally-driven Chromium (process management plus a CDP client covering navigate, click, evaluate, cookie jar, and CSP-violation observation) and a TLS-test client variant with self-signed acceptance. Then port C02/C03 fully against production behavior with no blocked legs and retire every runner. The migration waits on this new surface.
criteria.defer_browser_queues: Leave C02/C03/C04 untouched (all 10 records: 2 .mjs runners, 3 .ts/.md files, 5 fixtures) and finish the other 6 remaining records first, returning to the browser queues only with fresh evidence or a changed mechanism set. No blocked legs are authored and no browser-driving surface is built; the migration completes around the deferred scope.
criteria.port_wire_with_blocked: Port every wire-observable leg to running Can now (in-process server, fetch_bytes, SQL descriptors; S04 fully; plain-HTTP equivalents where TLS is incidental; sequential approximations with visible blocked legs for races), convert C02/C03 fixture reads to the C01 producer, retire the five C04 fixture files, and record the real-browser enforcement legs plus TLS-listener legs as explicit blocked legs with named missing primitives. The .mjs/.ts runners stay until their blocked legs clear; no new runtime surface is built.

browser_scope.instructions: Which scope should the C02/C03/C04 browser migration take so the 28-record migration reaches its goal with honest verdicts and without stranding coverage?

state.baselines: Four browser-queue baselines remain: tests/site_delivery/proof.mjs (171 lines, 9 PASS groups, Playwright plus Chromium plus self-signed TLS via openssl), tests/site_delivery/strict-redirect.mjs (90 lines), tests/site_preview/probe.ts S03 (279 lines: Can issuance plus SQLite plus HTTPS plus browser), tests/site_preview/approval_probe.ts S04 (168 lines: plain HTTP plus SQLite plus file staging, no browser, no TLS). C01 (fixture producer) is done; C04 retires 5 fixture files after C02/C03 switch reads.
state.browser_only_legs: No Can mechanism exists for: JavaScript execution and DOM/CSS/font/media evaluation (fixtureReady, getComputedStyle, fonts.ready, image decode, clicks), real cookie-jar semantics (__Host- prefix, HttpOnly, SameSite, redirect carriage, forge resistance), Content-Security-Policy enforcement reporting (securitypolicyviolation), navigation and referrer defaults plus authored overrides, worker/serviceworker blocking. proof.mjs needs these for about 5 of 9 groups; strict-redirect.mjs for the form-action block and click-chain cookie legs; probe.ts lines 227-277 (2 groups).
state.mandate: Can is an AI-agent-authored language with no backwards-compatibility obligations; the standing rule prefers reaching the migration goal over scaffolding and nested proof layers. The migration checklist owns exactly 28 baseline records in manolea-2/tests with per-file retirement gates: a host harness retires only when its retained legs pass as running Can verdicts against production behavior (F01 reconciliation). The machine is a 256 GB MacBook; disk and load are hard constraints.
state.mechanism_inventory: The catalogue holds 44 browser:: operations covering in-process DOM emulation (mount, query, events, state); zero cover navigation, cookie jars, network issuance, TLS, CDP, or external browser control (verified by catalogue grep). http::fetch_bytes (qualified 2026-10-02, live 13/13) covers plain-HTTP wire legs including ?query repeats and manual redirects. Twelve of 28 records are fulfilled with this exact mechanism set; no port has needed browser driving so far.
state.portable_legs: Most checks are wire-observable and portable to the proven in-process pattern (staged production site_routes plus server_start/stop, http::fetch_bytes client, probe-owned SQL descriptors, /usr/bin/sqlite3 for DDL): grant/claim/303 chains, set-cookie wire values, header text (CSP, referrer-policy, cache-control), status codes, SQLite grant/expiry/revocation/state rows, file integrity, restart persistence. S04 is fully portable modulo one mount decision (its exchange() calls the TypeScript createPreviewHandler in-process; the Can port must mount an equivalent Can production preview route, pending confirmation one exists). The S03 Promise.all single-use race becomes sequential second-claim-denied plus a visible blocked simultaneity leg.
state.tls_position: Server-side TLS exists (http::server_start_tls); the client side cannot accept the baselines' self-signed certificates: Bun fetch rejects them ('self signed certificate', verified 2026-10-02) and http::fetch_bytes exposes no insecure or test-CA option. openssl is available for minting fixture certificates via process::run. The S03 TLS-wire legs are transport-incidental (identical assertions would pass over plain HTTP); only 'serves correctly over a TLS listener' itself is TLS-specific and would reduce to a bind-only leg.
